messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: vectorizing code
parts:
Hi, I’m trying to fit ordered logit with a certain kind of fake-data prior. See Stan model (and test R code) below. I got it to run but with a loop. Commented out in the Stan model is the code that did not work.

Here’s my question: is there a way to vectorize out the “for (n in 1:N)” loop in the model?

Thanks.
Andrew

—

Stan program (ordered_logit.stan)

data {
int<lower=2> K;
int<lower=0> N;
int<lower=1> M;
int<lower=1,upper=K> y[N];
matrix[N,M] X;
real<lower=0> prior_size;
}
parameters {
vector[M] beta;
ordered[K-1] c;
}
model {
for (n in 1:N){
y[n] ~ ordered_logistic(X[n]*beta,c);
for (k in 1:K){
increment_log_prob(ordered_logistic_log(k,X[n]*beta,c)*prior_size/(N*K));
}
}
// y ~ ordered_logistic(X*beta, c);
// for (k in 1:K){
// increment_log_prob(ordered_logistic_log(k,X*beta,c)*prior_size/(N*K));
// }
}

—

R script:

N <- 100
M <- 3
K <- 5
X <- array(rnorm(N*M), c(N,M))
y <- sample(1:K, N, replace=TRUE)
prior_size <- 1

library("rstan")
ol <- stan("ordered_logit.stan", data=list(N=N,M=M,K=K,X=X,y=y,prior_size=prior_size), iter=100, chains=4)
print(ol)

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: vectorizing code
parts:
The ordered_logistic function currently only accepts an integer as its first argument, rather than an array of integers like bernoulli_logit. But there is no real reason why it should have this limitation.

Ben
